reason: The observation measures out; the fix is broken at three of the five widths it claims to cover, and it breaks the one composition the source explicitly protects. MEASURED (chromium, ?v=light&state=first-run&motion=settled). At 1440 the card is 1084x268.9 at 206->1290, .hero resolves to 300px 686px with a 48px gap, .hero-fig 231->531, .chart 579->1265, and .cols/.baseline/.plot.solo~.xaxis all clamped to 579->636. So the 629px figure is real, but it is the distance from the baseline's right edge to the chart's right edge, not 'from the right edge of the only painted mark': the rightmost painted thing is the .bar-val label '12 so far', 68.3px wide, running to 647.3, which leaves 618.7px to the card's inner edge (1266) - 57% of the card, not 58%. That 68.3 matters, because it is the number the fix gets wrong. THE FIX, DRIVEN. Rule 1, `[data-state="first-run"] .hero { grid-template-columns: minmax(220px,300px) auto; }`, has specificity (0,2,0) and the phone rule at lately.html:554, `.hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }` inside `@media (max-width:900px)`, has (0,1,0). A media query does not add specificity, so the stacked hero never comes back. Injected and measured, the computed grid at 900 is `300px 86px`, at 768 `300px 86px`, at 560 `300px 102px`, at 390 `252px 32px` - two columns at every width. The finding's claim that 'at 900 and below the existing stacked grid takes over' is false, and the phone composition argued at lately.html:549-553 ('Not a reduction: the hero stacks so the numeral keeps its scale') is deleted by rule 1 alone. At 390 it is not merely different, it is broken: .cols keeps its fixed 57px inside a 32px track and the card reports scrollWidth-clientWidth = 20; captured, the hatched column, the '12 SO FAR' label and the '13 JUL' tick are all sliced by the card's right border. Nothing catches it downstream - .scroll is `overflow-x: clip`, so document overflow still reads 0 and the gate's overflow probes stay green while the only mark on the state hangs off the card. Rule 2's arithmetic is wrong too. '24+300+48+57+24 = 453 in a 460 box' sizes the chart track to the 57px column, but every mark in .plot.solo is absolutely positioned, so the track's content width comes from the 57px .xaxis and `auto` then stretches under normal justify-content: measured at 1440 the track is 62px, the card is exactly 460, and the .bar-val label runs to 647.3 against an inner edge of 642 - the label sits inside the right padding with 18.7px of gutter, not 24. The 460 box does not contain the content it was sized for. On severity: even with a working fix this is a refinement, not a defect. Nothing is wrong, unreadable or untrue here - the sparseness is the honest consequence of two protected decisions (no ghost slots, no scale from one datum), the mark carries its own value and its own date within 68px of itself after the r2 fix, and a wide card with air on its right is a density judgment a studio could take either way. On a frozen closing round that is not worth moving a pixel with a rule that costs the phone.
sharpenedFix: If the studio does want the card sized to its content, the rule must be fenced above the stack breakpoint and sized to the label, not to the column: `@media (min-width: 901px) { [data-state="first-run"] .hero { grid-template-columns: minmax(220px, 300px) 72px; } [data-state="first-run"] .card.hero { width: max-content; max-width: 100%; } }`. 72px clears the 68.3px '12 so far' label so the 24px right gutter survives; `width: max-content` lets the card be 24+300+48+72+24 = 468 rather than guessing 460; `max-width: 100%` keeps it inside the band; and the 901 floor leaves the stacked phone hero, the 560 rules and the 390 card exactly as they ship. Even so, this is a taste change on a frozen surface, not a correction.
breaks: Rule 1 as filed silently overrides `@media (max-width:900px) .hero { grid-template-columns: 1fr }` by specificity and clips the mark, its value and its tick out of the card at 390 with `overflow-x: clip` hiding the evidence from every document-level overflow probe. If any version of this lands, re-measure: (a) the computed `grid-template-columns` on .hero at 901/900/793/768/560/390 for first-run AND for full, to prove the phone stack is untouched; (b) the card's scrollWidth-clientWidth and the right edge of `.plot.solo .bar-val` and of `.plot.solo ~ .xaxis span` against `.card.hero` right at every one of those widths - the existing 'no week tick leaves the card' assertion at interaction-check.mjs:749-764 runs only for state 'full', so it cannot see this and should be extended to first-run and to .bar-val; (c) the ages-card rung gap assertion (interaction-check.mjs ~line 740) for first-run, since the hero card's height drops from 483.8 to 268.9 at 768/900 and from 467.8 to 252.9 at 560/390; (d) the .rise entrance and focus-ring inset at the new card edge; and (e) the dark twin at 1440 and 390, since nothing here was measured on the flipped ground.
